themes.name: Security work packaged for coding agents

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Today’s strongest momentum clusters around agent workflows and agent-facing tools: Claude-BugHunter leads the signal set with +2,037 stars, while Superpowers, CLI-Anything, and several other agent projects also drew substantial gains. Web data, media production, model training, and local-first productivity round out the picture.

sections.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter
sections.description: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work, with vulnerability-class skills, disclosed-report patterns, and enterprise attack matrices.
sections.why_notable: The highest signal score (9.120) and largest daily gain (+2,037); its README describes a modular, scope-conscious security workflow built from installable skills and commands.
sections.unique_caveat: Designed as a Claude Code skill bundle; the README describes its own plugin and copy-install paths.

sections.title: XiaoYouChR/Ghost-Downloader-3
sections.description: A cross-platform downloader supporting multiple protocols and media sources.
sections.why_notable: Second-highest signal score (8.484) and +1,078 stars; the README distinguishes it with a single desktop workflow spanning HTTP, BitTorrent, FTP, streaming formats, video sites, and browser handoff.

sections.title: firecrawl/firecrawl
sections.description: Web data infrastructure for agents, with search, scraping, and access to data providers.
sections.why_notable: The +920 gain and 8.325 score put it among the strongest signals; its README presents a three-way design—local binary, hosted cloud, or self-hosted server—with MCP/API interfaces.
sections.unique_caveat: The local MCP setup documented in the README requires Node.js 22+; local browser rendering has an additional browser dependency.

sections.title: zhouxiaoka/autoclip
sections.description: An open-source AI video clipping and content-repurposing desktop tool for turning long videos into short-form edits.
sections.why_notable: A +908 gain and 8.312 score signal strong interest in end-to-end creator tooling; the README says desktop, CLI, and MCP workflows produce video, subtitles, covers, and publishing copy.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says the desktop software is free but cloud models are billed by usage.

sections.title: obra/superpowers
sections.description: An agentic skills framework and software-development methodology for coding agents.
sections.why_notable: Its +838 gain and 8.232 score keep agent-development workflows near the top; the README emphasizes a gated sequence of specification, approved design, implementation planning, TDD, and subagent execution across multiple harnesses.

sections.title: jingyaogong/minimind
sections.description: A small, from-scratch language-model training project designed to make the training pipeline accessible.
sections.why_notable: The +828 gain and 8.220 score mark practical model-building as a parallel theme; its README exposes a broad learning path from pretraining and SFT through fine-tuning, preference optimization, tool use, and distillation.
sections.unique_caveat: The README clarifies that the advertised two hours refers to one SFT epoch on a single NVIDIA 3090, not the full training lifecycle.

sections.title: mvanhorn/last30days-skill
sections.description: An AI-agent research skill that searches social, video, community, prediction-market, and web sources.
sections.why_notable: The +790 gain and 8.173 score point to demand for agent-driven research synthesis; the README frames its differentiator as scoring discussion signals rather than relying only on editorial selection.

sections.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything
sections.description: A project aiming to make software usable through agent-native command-line interfaces.
sections.why_notable: The +783 gain and 8.164 score reinforce the agent-tooling cluster; its central premise is to expose existing software through CLI surfaces that coding agents can operate.

sections.title: mjmirza/app-store-compliance
sections.description: A playbook and pre-submission guard for App Store and Google Play review requirements.
sections.why_notable: A +755 gain on a relatively small signal total (4,815) gives it a strong score of 8.128; it brings policy checks and compliance knowledge into agent-assisted app development.
sections.unique_caveat: Its README explicitly says the scan cannot guarantee store approval and that some checks still require human review.

sections.title: cathrynlavery/diagram-design
sections.description: An agent skill for producing editorial diagrams as self-contained HTML and SVG.
sections.why_notable: Its +624 gain and 7.938 score make design tooling a visible supporting theme; the README differentiates it with 52 diagram types and a single-file HTML/SVG output.

sections.title: toeverything/AFFiNE
sections.description: A privacy-focused, local-first knowledge workspace combining documents, whiteboards, and planning.
sections.why_notable: A +593 gain and 7.887 score provide a counterpoint to the agent-heavy list: interest also reaches a user-facing, local-first productivity suite.

sections.title: Tracer-Cloud/opensre
sections.description: A self-hosted CLI agent for diagnosing CI/CD failures and proposing fixes.
sections.why_notable: Its +438 gain and 7.584 score show infrastructure operations joining the agent trend; the README describes a reviewable flow from failed run to diagnosis and proposed fix.
sections.unique_caveat: The repository labels the project public alpha.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content:
- **Agent workflows and agent-facing software:** Claude-BugHunter, Superpowers, CLI-Anything, and App Store Compliance turn security, development methodology, software control, or policy knowledge into structured tools for coding agents.
- **Agent infrastructure and research:** Firecrawl targets web ingestion for agents; Last30days-skill packages cross-source research synthesis; OpenSRE applies an agent to CI/CD diagnosis and proposed fixes.
- **Practical AI creation:** MiniMind makes model-training code inspectable, while AutoClip automates long-to-short video production.
- **Beyond agents:** Ghost Downloader combines multiple download protocols in a desktop utility; AFFiNE represents local-first knowledge work; Diagram Design focuses on agent-assisted visual output.
- **Languages:** Python appears in 7 of the 12 selected repos, TypeScript in 2, Shell in 2, and HTML in 1 (GitHub primary-language labels).

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The snapshot suggests the strongest appetite is for agent systems that make work operational—repeatable workflows, software interfaces, research access, and security or reliability tasks—rather than for a single model release. At the same time, meaningful gains for creator, desktop, and local-first workspace tools show the trend is spreading into end-user workflows.
